intro: A TV cooking contest: who takes part, what the rounds are, and how to tell it with the passive voice.
p.jurado.consejo: The j sounds like h: «hu-RA-do». It is a group, but it takes the singular: «el jurado decide».
p.presentador.consejo: The feminine is «presentadora». They present the show and talk to the guests.
p.finalista.consejo: It works for men and women: «el finalista», «la finalista». It is who reaches the last round.
p.favorito.consejo: Feminine: «la favorita». It is also an adjective: «mi plato favorito» is the one I like best.
p.aficionado.consejo: Feminine: «aficionada». It comes from «afición». It is the opposite of «profesional».
p.prueba.consejo: It also means «proof»: «no hay pruebas». It comes from «probar».
p.reto.consejo: The first r is strong: «RRE-to». You say «aceptar un reto» or «superar un reto».
p.ensayo.consejo: You say «hacer un ensayo» and «ensayar». It is also a short opinion text.
p.semifinal.consejo: It has «semi-» (half): «semifinal», «semicírculo». After the semifinal comes the final.
p.clasificación.consejo: It ends in «-ción», like «puntuación». It comes from «clasificar»: to sort into groups.
p.plato.consejo: It is also the object you serve food on. «Un plato típico» is a traditional dish.
p.postre.consejo: It is masculine: «el postre». You say «de postre tomo fruta».
p.eliminar.consejo: It is regular. In the passive: «fue eliminado». You can also eliminate a stain or a mistake.
p.premiar.consejo: You say «premiar con un viaje». The stressed syllable is the last one: «pre-MYAR».
b1.titulo: From the first round to the prize
b1.texto:
**Who takes part.** In a cooking contest there are **concursantes**, a **jurado** and a **presentador** or presentadora. The **favorito** is the one most people expect to win; the **aficionado** follows the show for fun.

**What happens.** Each **prueba** is a **reto**: a **plato** or **postre** with little time. Before that there are **ensayos**. After the **semifinal**, the **finalistas** reach the final.

**The result.** The **clasificación** says who is ahead. One person is **eliminado**; another is **premiado** with a trip.

**The passive voice.** In the news you often hear **ser + participle**: **fue elegido**, **ha sido premiada**, **será anunciado**. The participle agrees with the subject. With **por** you say who does the action.
b2.f0.texto: Tonight the jury will choose the two finalists.
b2.f1.texto: I rehearsed this dessert every night.
b2.f2.texto: Your dessert is the audience's favourite.
b2.f3.texto: Today's round will be a challenge without a recipe.
b2.f4.texto: If they eliminate me, I will try again next year.
b2.f5.texto: The ranking will be published after the last round.
b2.f6.texto: The winner will be awarded a trip to Lisbon.
b2.f7.texto: Last night's rehearsal has given me a lot of confidence.
b4.texto:
**Ser + participle** puts the person or thing that receives the action first: **El postre fue elegido por el jurado.** The participle agrees with the subject: **elegido**, **elegida**, **elegidos**, **elegidas**.

- With **por** you say who does the action (the agent): **por el jurado**.
- It is used in every tense: **fue elegido**, **ha sido elegido**, **será elegido**.
- **Estar + participle** is not passive: it tells the result. **El postre está terminado.**

In daily speech the **reflexive passive** with **se** is very common: **Se anunciará el nombre del ganador.**
b4.e0.texto: The dessert was chosen by the jury.
b4.e1.texto: The finalists will be announced tonight.
b4.e2.texto: The name of the winner will be announced in May.
b5.f0.texto: The studio lights warmed the air with a white glare.
b5.f1.texto: On the counters the knives gleamed like small mirrors.
b5.f2.texto: The contestant stirred the sauce with a wooden spoon and breathed deeply.
b5.f3.texto: A drop of caramel fell slowly from the edge of the pan.
b5.f4.texto: Behind the cameras, his brother smiled at him in silence.
b5.f5.texto: The three members of the jury cut the dessert with a thin knife.
b5.f6.texto: The cream sank slowly like a tired cloud.
b5.f7.texto: A murmur of disappointment ran through the studio from end to end.
b5.f8.texto: The host asked for silence with her hands raised.
b5.f9.texto: The other finalist asked to repeat the round because the oven had failed on the first attempt.
b6.o0.refuerzo: It is active: the jury does the action.
b6.o1: El postre fue elegido por el jurado
b6.o1.refuerzo: Yes: ser + participle, and «por» says who acts.
b6.o2: El postre está en el horno
b6.o2.refuerzo: There is no participle: «está» only says where.
b6.pregunta: Which of these sentences is in the passive voice?
b7.o0.refuerzo: It is singular; «los finalistas» is plural.
b7.o1.refuerzo: It is feminine; «los finalistas» is masculine here.
b8.frase: El postre fue elegido por el jurado
b8.traduccion: The dessert was chosen by the jury
b9.o0.refuerzo: Yes: «un ensayo» is practice before the real performance.
b9.o1.refuerzo: «Un reto» is something hard you have to overcome.
b9.o2.refuerzo: It is the list that says who is ahead.
b9.pregunta: What is practising before the real round called?
b11.frase: El ganador será premiado ____ un viaje.
b11.o0.refuerzo: «Premiar» does not take «a» before the prize.
b11.o1.refuerzo: Yes: «premiar con» a trip, «premiar con» a trophy.
b11.o2.refuerzo: «Por» gives the reason: «premiado por su receta».
b11.pregunta: Which preposition does «premiar» take before the prize?
b12.o0.refuerzo: The host runs the show on the set.
b12.o1.refuerzo: The finalist competes in the last round.
b12.o2.refuerzo: Yes: the fan follows the show for pleasure, without competing.
b12.pregunta: Who follows the contest from home out of interest?
p.elegirá.consejo: Future of «elegir», third person: the «á» marks the future.
p.finalistas.consejo: Plural of «finalista», someone who reaches the last round.
p.ensayé.consejo: Past tense of «ensayar» for «yo»: the accent on the «é» marks it.
p.eliminan.consejo: Third person plural of «eliminar», to remove or knock out.
p.volveré.consejo: Future of «volver» for «yo»: the «é» marks the future.
p.intentarlo.consejo: The infinitive «intentar» with «lo» attached; the stress stays on «tar».
p.publicará.consejo: Future of «publicar», third person: the «á» marks the future.
p.premiado.consejo: Past participle of «premiar», to give a prize.
p.elegido.consejo: Past participle of «elegir»; the «g» sounds like «h».
p.anunciados.consejo: Past participle of «anunciar» in the plural; it agrees with the nouns.
p.anunciará.consejo: Future of «anunciar», third person: the «á» marks the future.
p.mayo.consejo: Months are written in lowercase in Spanish.
p.focos.consejo: A «foco» is a lamp that lights a stage or a studio.
p.estudio.consejo: «Estudio» can mean study or studio; here it is the recording room.
p.calentaban.consejo: Imperfect of «calentar» for «ellos»: the action went on in the past.
p.resplandor.consejo: A strong light that dazzles, from «resplandecer».
p.encimeras.consejo: Plural of «encimera», the flat surface in a kitchen where you cook.
p.cuchillos.consejo: Plural of «cuchillo»; the «ch» sounds like «ch» in «church».
p.removía.consejo: Imperfect of «remover»; the «í» breaks the diphthong: re-mo-BI-a.
p.salsa.consejo: «Salsa» is a sauce; it can also be the music and dance.
p.respiraba.consejo: Imperfect of «respirar»: an action that went on in the past.
p.gota.consejo: A «gota» is a drop of liquid, like a drop of rain.
p.caramelo.consejo: Caramel is sugar cooked until golden.
p.caía.consejo: The «í» breaks the diphthong: ka-I-a, in two syllables.
p.sonreía.consejo: Imperfect of «sonreír»; the «í» means two syllables.
p.miembros.consejo: Plural of «miembro», a person who belongs to a group.
p.cortaron.consejo: Third person plural of «cortar» in the past.
p.cuchillo.consejo: The «ll» in Spain sounds like «y»: cu-CHI-yo.
p.hundió.consejo: Third person of «hundir» in the past: it went down.
p.decepción.consejo: «Decepción» comes from «decepcionar», to let someone down.
p.extremo.consejo: «Extremo» is the far end or edge of something.
p.presentadora.consejo: Feminine of «presentador», the person who hosts a show.
p.repetir.consejo: Infinitive of «repetir», to do or say again.
p.fallado.consejo: Past participle of «fallar», to fail or break down.
